featured_reviews.name: Akhil Vaidya
featured_reviews.review_text: Gurukripa is a great spot in Sion offering a wide variety of snacks and sweets at affordable prices (around ₹200–₹300 per person). While everything is decent, their samosa truly stands out crispy, flavorful, and absolutely worth trying. It’s no surprise that Gurukripa is well-known for its samosas, which are widely supplied to cinemas and theatres across the city. Definitely recommended for a quick and tasty bite!

featured_reviews.name: Desii Thing
featured_reviews.review_text:
I would have easily given 5 stars, but recently the overall taste seems to have gone slightly down compared to what it used to be.

Still, the samosa with chutney and chole remains their signature and is absolutely worth trying — crisp, flavourful, and perfectly balanced. The gulab jamun is also soft, rich, and makes a great finish to the meal.

They have a wide variety of chaats, North Indian snacks, sweets, and quick bites — most items are decent in quality and value for money. Service is fast, and this place continues to be a popular local landmark with a loyal fan following over the years.

Only minor downsides are the slightly toned-down spice and taste recently, limited seating comfort, and parking challenges due to the busy area.

Overall, still one of the must-try classic spots in Mumbai for samosa-chole lovers — just wish they bring back their old flavour punch!

featured_reviews.review_text:
I’m a pure non-vegetarian, yet this vegetarian restaurant is my absolute favorite—life truly is full of paradoxes! I’ve been coming here for the last 20 years and still counting. Needless to say, the best dishes are tikki-chole, samosa-chole, lassi, and the mini cheese samosas. They also offer good low-sugar sweet options for people on a diet.
I still remember waiting an hour for an AC seat with friends during our college days—and we would happily wait just for the food. For those who complain about the wait, good things take time. Every visit here feels purely nostalgic.

featured_reviews.name: Vedant Naik
featured_reviews.review_text:
Pathetic Service..!!

Visited A1 Samosa today, a place many people know for its iconic aloo samosas. While the regular aloo samosa lives up to its reputation, the overall customer experience was disappointing.

I purchased 12 samosas and specifically requested them to be packed in two separate bags due to the quantity. The staff ignored the request and packed everything into a single bag without any consideration.

The bigger issue came after I reached home and counted the order—there were only 11 samosas instead of the 12 I paid for. Since I live far away, returning to the shop wasn't practical.

Another disappointment was their flavored/variant samosas. The stuffing quantity was surprisingly low and did not justify the price at all. It honestly felt like poor value for money. Apart from the regular aloo samosa, I would not recommend any of the other variants.

A good product can bring customers in, but poor service, inaccurate orders, and an indifferent attitude can leave a lasting negative impression. The owners should pay attention to staff behavior, order accuracy, and customer experience. This is a classic example of a great product being let down by worst service and management.

If you're visiting, try the regular aloo samosa. For everything else, manage your expectations.

Disappointed customer experience.

featured_reviews.name: imran badami
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a samosa lover like me, then A1 Samosa in Mumbai is an absolute must-visit! Hands down one of the best samosa spots in the city and easily one of my all-time favorites.

What I love most? The incredible variety they offer — but the star of my show has got to be their corn and cheese samosa. Crispy, cheesy, with just the right touch of sweetness from the corn — pure magic!

The service here is super fast and friendly, which is impressive given how packed this place always is. Yep, it’s so popular that you’ll almost definitely have to wait, but trust me, it’s totally worth it.

At A1 Samosa, samosas aren’t just a snack — they’re the whole experience! If you’re in Mumbai and craving some serious samosa goodness, you know where to go.

featured_reviews.name: Florence Vegas
featured_reviews.review_text: A1 Samosa is very famous in Mumbai however I think it's overhyped. The taste is good but the Samosa size is small and they charge for chutney. I think this is the first place I visited who charged me for chutney.

featured_reviews.name: HB
featured_reviews.review_text:
A1 Samosa is a well-known spot for quick, tasty snacks and lives up to its reputation for serving consistently good samosas. The samosas are crisp on the outside with a well-spiced, flavourful filling inside, served hot and fresh. The balance of spices is just right—neither too mild nor overly spicy—making them enjoyable for a wide range of tastes.

What adds to the experience is the freshness and speed of service, even during busy hours. The accompanying chutneys complement the samosas nicely and enhance the overall flavour. The place itself is simple and functional, focused more on food quality than ambience. Overall, A1 Samosa is a reliable stop for anyone craving classic, well-made samosas at a reasonable price.

featured_reviews.review_text: Rating only for Samosa - Earlier A1 Samosa used to be my favorite, but lately they have really downgraded their quality and taste. featured_reviews.name: Prashant
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you love Chole Bhature, this place is a must-try!
Visited this place recently and had a good overall experience. The chole bhature here are definitely a highlight. I tried the chole cheese bhature and it was very satisfying. The Amritsari kulcha was also good and worth trying. Overall, it’s definitely worth the money.
That said, the place has a few practical limitations. There are no washroom facilities, parking can be quite difficult to find, and there’s no wheelchair-accessible parking. The surrounding area is usually crowded with slow-moving traffic and narrow roads, so reaching and parking can take some effort.
If you’re okay with these inconveniences, it’s a great spot for tasty North Indian street-style food.

featured_reviews.name: Alok Misra
featured_reviews.review_text: Literally a Hole in the wall but with amazing and authentic food. The chole bhature and Amritsari Kulchas (made in the tandoor) were to die for. Both come with unlimited refills of the delicious chole. This is in the lane leading up to Dashmesh Gurudwara. Parking is a problem so best to Uber it. Some street parking on the main road. We went on a Sunday so the faithful were thronging to the Gurudwara. We saw a cross section of patrons at this place - many seemed like regulars. Folks were also getting takeaway (as did we) and orders from platforms were also flying in. The owner is a nice friendly person and quite chatty as well. The setting is pretty much a classic dhaba type with very basic tables and chairs and a few fans (non there were no manjis!). We will be back for more but once the weather gets hotter it may just be for takeaway. Also this place serves only vegetarian food and also has jain options (priced extra)

featured_reviews.name: Sourajyoti
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sardar Paya House in Sion is famous for its paya and it truly lives up to the hype. The goat paya here is slow-cooked, rich, and full of flavour, with soft meat and a thick, spicy gravy. It tastes best with roti or pao (Maharashtrian bun).
The place is simple and no-frills, but the food is what matters. Service is quick and prices are reasonable. If you love traditional Mumbai-style non-veg and good paya, this is a must-visit.

I tried paya for the first time—the taste was decent, but I can’t compare it since I don’t know how it’s supposed to taste.
The timings are 11:30 to 5:30

featured_reviews.name: Nancy Kumar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Went here last evening, easy to find, close to Sion station. Gets crowded in the evening, even on weekdays. Since it's is located so close to the station, looks like a popular place to have a drink and dinner.
Seating on the ground and first floor. First floor is air conditioned.
Food is good, I would recommend bombil fry, mandeli fry and the people at the next table recommended the crispy veg fry, which was also very good.
Because of the location and affordable rates, this place can be a bit packed. One would have to wait for a seat. Seating is really small, about 3_4 people only at each table. Except the last table where about 5_6 people can be crammed.
Service is quick because of high turnover at the tables.
Gents washroom is on the ground floor of the restaurant, whereas  ladies would have to go to the back of the building where the washeoon is.
Our group had a very nice time here, but could have been better if the place was a bit more roomy.

customer_updates.name: Yatendra Singh
customer_updates.text: I was a little underwhelmed by the breakfast selection at this place, particularly given the price point. However, I must say that the pancakes with maple syrup were delicious, and the omelette was a real treat. The ambience of the restaurant was stunning, which added to the overall experience. They had a wide variety of tea cakes to choose from. They also had diverse range of Indian dishes, including dosa, idli, chole bhature, sabudana khichdi, aalo paratha etc. On the downside, the bacon was a disappointment as it was overcooked and difficult to chew. Nevertheless, the staff were incredibly polite and accommodating.

featured_reviews.name: Maheep Singh
featured_reviews.review_text: One needs to be ready for a little waiting time,but it is rewarding and worth one's patience. We asked for Tandoori Chicken and Mr. Jaswinder S Oberoi helped us to make the right decision by suggesting have half of both varieties, HP Special and Chatpata Tandoori. Both were lip smacking and scrumptious.  Then, we asked for Fish Amritsari fry, the pieces were big, succulent, tasty served with lacha onion. We skipped the main course but enjoyed the Gulab Jamun with rabdi. Gopal and Muktiram were our hosts and served us very well. All together it was a great evening spent and it was value for money 😋🤤

Hardeep Punjab - A Treat for Tandoori Lovers!
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Visited Hardeep Punjab recently and was truly impressed by the flavors and the variety! We ordered the Non-Veg Platter, and it was a feast of smoky, juicy, and perfectly marinated delights. The platter included creamy chicken tikka, spicy seekh kebabs, prawns, and fish, each one cooked to perfection. The chutneys and pickled onions served alongside added that extra punch.

The menu offers a wide range of non-veg appetizers – from Chaska Maska Tikka to Thai Tikka – and everything sounded tempting. The place has a nostalgic charm with its classic Punjabi touch, established since 1988, and it's clear why it’s a favorite in the area.

Service was quick, portions were generous, and the taste was genuinely authentic. Whether you're with friends or family, this is a solid place to enjoy rich Punjabi flavors.

Must-try: Non-Veg Platter, Prawns Lasooni Tikka, and Chicken Lollipop
Will definitely be back to explore more from the menu!

featured_reviews.name: Divyani
featured_reviews.review_text:
Went to Hardeep Punjab for a family dinner, we had their Chicken Manchow Soup, masala chicken lollipop, Chicken tikka biryani (no matka) and Dal fry & jeera rice.

They also served us with variety of side dishes (peanuts, chakli, fried noodles) for timepass and onion, pickles, etc.

The food portion was good, food was tasty and would definitely go again.

Do try their matka biryani options for an experience.

Post dinner, they served sauf, sweet imli candies and jaggery instead of sugar which was the plus point.

Also, make sure you avoid sitting next to the washroom.

featured_reviews.name: Reet Garkel
featured_reviews.review_text: The quality of the food amd service has deteriorated!!!! The waiters & service helpers were extremely non attentive & too rude. Washroom was sooo dirty- somebody had puked in there & it was unclean. The food & ambience used to genuinely be great & fun however now the quality has gone down. Special remarks for the waiters from Jharkhand; particularly rude as they didn’t serve us the food and did not bring the drinks on time after persistently reminding them!!! They also kept asking for tips and opened the bill book for us as if we are responsible for paying them. Someone who didn’t even serve us was expecting us to pay them a tip. The service helpers were fighting with each other right infront of us. Quite disappointed !!!

featured_reviews.name: VINAY Ashok ASARPOTA
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had ordered beer 🍺 and Soft drink with Chicken Tandoori. Don't recommend buying Drinks as they overcharged, three times the price! Absolutely NOTHING SERVED WITH BEER, NOBODY CARED TO ASK ! Deducted a star from SERVICE.
They served full Chicken Tandoori but didn't CARED TO ASK if wanted in pieces or without pieces!
Tandoori Chicken was Buttered but Hardly noticeable.Was Cooked Properly, butBeing situated in Koliwada, surrounded by alot of Non Veg eateries its Not worth the price, as there are Excellent places which charge you alot less and Don't overcharge clients for Drinks!
Excellent Mango Pickle, Okay Mint Chutney unfortunately. Chaat masala was below average.
Was seated right under the A/c, A/c were not adequately cooling. The single TV is too small for the spacious Premise.
Biryani here is Served Spicier than Persian/Iranian/Muslim Restaurants. They spread the biryani gravy/masala upon entire rice. Looks like Chinese rice preparation style but Mixing with entire rice instead of Half of each biryani and rice, this way of Serving is Better.
